prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: how many price points does product 5 have? Every list price version of product 5 in price_history and every competitor price check of product 5 in competitor_prices is one price point, even when two of them have the same price. Return one column, price_points, the number of price points, in one row. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, look at the set operator inside the CTE: the count is lower than the number of rows in the two tables together.
UNION removes duplicate rows, so two price points with the same price count once. The question counts every row of both tables.
starter_sql:
WITH price_points AS (
  SELECT list_price_eur AS price_eur
  FROM price_history
  WHERE product_id = 5
  UNION
  SELECT price_eur
  FROM competitor_prices
  WHERE product_id = 5
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS price_points
FROM price_points
why_this_works: UNION ALL keeps the price points that share a price, so COUNT(*) counts every list price version and every check.
